Abbey combines a chat-first terminal interface, command-line workflows, provider
integration, persistent memory, and bounded local application services. The
existing application is **version 2.6**, written in **Rust 2024** with the
repository's exact **Rust 1.99.1** toolchain. Its desktop client is a member of
the same Cargo workspace, not a second authority over tools or user data.

[Install](#install) · [Quick use](#quick-use) · [Backends](#backends) ·
[Memory](#memory-backends) · [Learning](#learning-without-invented-training) ·
[Capability limits](#honest-limits) · [Documentation](#documentation)

## Abbey, LYLX, and the surrounding projects

**LYLX by The Donald Company** is the new ground-up intelligence program.
Quesar is its designated largest shared foundation model; Abbey and Aviva are
the consolidated personality direction; ABI provides dynamic moderation,
routing, and authorized execution; WDBX 3D supplies neural memory and storage.

This repository remains the existing Abbey application. Its provider adapters,
legacy Abbey/Aviva/Abi profile contracts, and local fixtures do **not** establish
that a production Quesar checkpoint has been trained or deployed. LYLX does not
silently replace existing code, stored data, or compatibility obligations.
Aviva's candid, minimally style-filtered mode changes expression, not tool
permissions, consent, privacy, or factual standards.

Related projects: [ABI](https://github.com/donaldfilimon/abi),
[WDBX](https://github.com/donaldfilimon/wdbx), and the
[quesar.cloud website](https://github.com/donaldfilimon/quesar.cloud).
The website and the Quesar model are distinct deliverables.

## Install

### Checkout and prerequisites

Preserve the sibling layout required by the path dependencies:

```text
workspace/
  abi/
  abbey/
  wdbx/
```

Use compatible sibling revisions; the repository's CI configuration records
its qualification pins. Cloning Abbey alone is not sufficient for resolving
all development and optional-feature dependencies. Read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)
for platform prerequisites and the current completion program.

On Unix/macOS, from the Abbey checkout:

```bash
./tools/cargo.sh build --locked -p abbey --release
./install.sh
abbey doctor
abbey claims
```

The wrapper keeps Cargo, rustc, rustdoc, rustfmt, and Clippy on the selected
toolchain even when another installation shadows PATH. The installer writes
`abbey` and `abbeyd` under `~/.local/bin` for the default edition.

The Windows installer is `powershell -File .\install.ps1`, targeting
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\abbey\bin`. Documented parser/naming checks are not evidence of
a live Windows installation; use the platform-specific status in the claims
ledger rather than assuming Unix behavior carries over.

The `personal-edition` feature selects separately named binaries and state
namespaces. It does not by itself add unrestricted shell execution. Preserve
existing allowlist/confirmation behavior until the separately specified local
execution path is implemented and qualified.

## Quick use

```bash
abbey                          # interactive TUI
abbey -c                       # continue a session
abbey exec "summarize src/"
abbey review
abbey doctor
abbey claims
abbey config --init            # scaffold configuration; never overwrite it
abbey memory map
abbey learn review
abbey learn stats
```

Generation requires a configured, available executor. Local metadata,
inventory, claims, and diagnostic commands do not require a generation backend.
Tool-bearing requests use the selected executor's capabilities and permission
model; describing a task does not guarantee successful execution.

In the TUI, **Ctrl-K** opens commands, **Ctrl-S** selects a provider, **Ctrl-B**
cycles installed providers, and **F1** shows keys. The composer is multiline.
Provider changes are blocked during an active run. See
[terminal reliability](docs/tui-reliability.md) for interruption and platform
boundaries.

## Backends

| Selection | Role and boundary |
| --- | --- |
| `ABBEY_BACKEND=ollama` | Preferred ready local provider; models are not silently downloaded. |
| `ABBEY_BACKEND=fm` | Apple Foundation Models CLI integration; `system` is on-device and explicitly selected `pcc` is off-device. Readiness is checked separately. |
| `ABBEY_BACKEND=abi` | Calls the sibling ABI executable. Local persona-template output is not a production Quesar model. |
| `ABBEY_BACKEND=claude` | Claude Code integration using its own installation, account, and session behavior. |
| `ABBEY_BACKEND=grok` | Grok Build integration. |
| `ABBEY_BACKEND=cursor` | Optional cursor-agent integration and supported tool/media surfaces. |

When no backend is explicitly chosen, the documented preference is ready local
Ollama, ready on-device `fm`, then installed `grok`, `abi`, `claude`, and finally
`cursor-agent`. The current Ollama default is `gemma4:26b-mlx`, with
`gemma:27b-mlx` as an alias; `abbey doctor` is the readiness check. An explicit
backend selection takes precedence. Provider names and model aliases are not
bundled Abbey weights or proof of response quality.

ABI integration requires a real executable, selected with `ABBEY_ABI_BIN` or
configuration; a shell alias is insufficient. Foundation Models integration
does not add an independent tool-execution engine. Live provider availability,
account authorization, and source-level wiring tests are separate evidence.

## Memory backends

SQLite is the default. The optional in-process WDBX backend is enabled at build
time with `--features wdbx` and selected with `ABBEY_MEMORY_BACKEND=wdbx` or the
corresponding configuration. The standard installer does not enable that
feature; an unavailable requested backend falls back to SQLite and is reported
by `abbey doctor`.

Memory records carry retention/provenance information. `abbey memory invalidate`
and `supersede` retire or replace records without silently deleting their
history. See the detailed memory documentation and command help before making
state-changing edits.

### The 3-D memory map

`abbey memory map` arranges records on **topic × recency × consolidation** axes.
This is a deterministic layout, **not a learned embedding space**, and visual
distance is not semantic similarity. It must not be confused with full WDBX 3D
Neural Specimen conformance.

### Semantic memory

Embeddings are a separate opt-in surface. The Apple and OpenAI-compatible
providers use explicitly selected model/dimension/revision spaces; incompatible
spaces are not compared, and provider failures do not silently choose another
provider. The documented external embedding payload contains summary and
subject tags, not raw payload or provenance. Review the configuration and data
boundary before enabling a remote provider.

## Learning without invented training

`abbey learn review` and `stats` curate `train_candidate` records. Teacher
responses and SFT export produce datasets, not optimizer steps. Local-first
teacher selection can include an explicitly identified off-device PCC fallback;
review provenance, privacy, and output-use rights before training on the result.

`abbey learn improve --apply` promotes routing changes, not foundation-model
weights. Quesar training, adapters, personality consolidation, and image/video
model qualification require their own artifacts, evaluations, and release
approval. A memory write or successful export is not evidence of those results.

## Authenticated application daemon

`abbeyd` exposes bounded, authenticated owner-only Unix services. Protocol-v1
reads, startup-bound protocol-v2 runs, and negotiated protocol-v3 capabilities
have distinct contracts. Model inventory, exact local lifecycle/inference
fixtures, approved memory effects, and sanitized memory reads are separately
qualified capabilities; none implies unrestricted remote execution.

Use [the current claims ledger](docs/claims.md) and
[runtime documentation](docs/runtime.md) for exact available operations,
startup authority, approval rules, and transport limits. Windows named pipes
and other unimplemented platform adapters must remain explicitly unavailable,
not simulated successes. The detailed daemon setup is preserved in the
[reference snapshot](README-REFERENCE-2026-10-25.md#authenticated-application-daemon).

## Media, thinking, generation, and tools

Image/video commands integrate with the selected supported external tool path;
the application does not ship general local image/video generation weights.
Generation must fail honestly when no usable tool exists. Mac voice commands
use installed platform voice/speech facilities and require the applicable
permissions; they are not a newly trained Abbey voice model.

MCP inventory, provider-specific management, ACP peers, and executor tools are
different surfaces. Listing a connector does not establish that it is installed,
authorized, or working. See the
[preserved command reference](README-REFERENCE-2026-10-25.md#media-thinking-generation-and-tools)
for detailed examples and provider limitations.

## Honest limits

The generated claims ledger above and [docs/claims.md](docs/claims.md) are the
capability authority. In particular, distinguish local peer processes from
multi-host execution; detected devices from executed kernels; a tiny model
fixture from production weights; and native compilation from live platform
acceptance. Do not promote proposals based on this README.

The safe and personal editions remain distinct. Approved future personal-shell
policy is not implemented permission to bypass current runtime checks. WDBX
privacy, erasure, and replication claims must retain their separately documented
scope rather than being inferred from a successful query.

## Verification and contribution

```bash
./check.sh
./desktop/check.sh
```

These are the documented application and desktop gates, not results from this
documentation change. Workspace defaults include the desktop members; a
package-only command is not equivalent to the full gate. Run applicable
checks on the required native platforms and report unavailable or skipped
checks explicitly. Never use live user stores for test fixtures.

The generated claims region is maintained by `tools/check_claims_sync.py`.
Change its source ledger, not the generated numbers by hand. Preserve the
[October 19 rewrite decision](REWRITE-DECISION-2026-10-19.md): Rust is the active
application and the canceled Zig rewrite must not be resumed inadvertently.
